title: A window in the scratch pane gets no frame callbacks after its first frame
body:
acre-gui is an eframe 0.37 app, and decade started it as its own window in the scratch pane with `scratch_open` and `terminal: false`. The window draws its first frame and then shows nothing new until the pane gets input. acre's issue acre-4db16b holds the trace.

A trace logged each call to eframe's `App::logic` and `App::ui`. `logic` ran every 250 to 750 ms, as the app's `request_repaint_after` asks. `ui` ran once, for the first frame. On Wayland, eframe calls `ui` only on winit's `RedrawRequested`, which waits for the compositor's frame callback. While no callback comes, eframe runs `logic` alone (`MISSED_REDRAW_TIMEOUT` in eframe's `src/native/run.rs`). So decade sends the window no frame callback after the first frame, though the window sits in a visible pane and keeps asking to redraw.

What a person sees: an app that changes on its own, such as one that reloads a file or animates, looks frozen until they click or type into it. A screenshot of the pane shows the stale first frame too.

To see it, start any eframe app that calls `request_repaint_after` in the scratch pane with `terminal: false`, change something it shows, and take a screenshot without touching the pane.
